issuer: the prefectural public safety commission (in Tokyo, the Metropolitan Police Department)
note: Read 2026-10-30. The Tokyo Metropolitan Police Department's page for taking the ordinary licence after a designated driving school gives the fee as ¥4,250 (an exam fee of ¥1,900 and a licence issuing fee of ¥2,350), the amount held (applying directly, without a school, costs more and needs a paid course, not held); its introduction page says a licence is issued from 18 (the test may be sat from 17½). The Road Traffic Act (道路交通法, e-Gov's current text) Article 95-6 makes a licence held by a driver in the '違反運転者等' class valid until a month after the third birthday after issue, and five for excellent and general drivers; the MPD's renewal page puts someone licensed for under five years on the first-renewal course, so a first licence is kept as 3 years. Fees are the prefecture's, set to the national standard; Tokyo's are the ones held. No identification card is issued by the licensing office (the My Number card is a municipality's).
